ety.text: From Proto-Italic *tardo-, from Proto-Indo-European *tr̥h₂-d-o-, from the root *terh₂- (“to cross over, pass through, overcome”). The phonetic development follows the regular Latin outcome of a syllabic liquid followed by a laryngeal (*r̥h₂ > -ar-). Semantically, the word likely shifted from "drawn out" or "taking a long time to cross/endure" to "slow" or "late". Cognate with Sanskrit तरति (tárati, “crosses over, overcomes”) and Ancient Greek τρανής (tranḗs, “piercing, clear, distinct”).
